last.verdict: Kodak's chemicals unit kept growing and generated cash, but a 7% drop in Print cut that unit's profit from $8M to $1M.

takeaways.label: Chemicals carries the company
takeaways.text: Advanced Materials & Chemicals revenue rose 21% to $99M and its operating profit rose to $21M from $16M. Management calls it Kodak's fastest-growing, most profitable unit.

takeaways.label: Print is weakening
takeaways.text: Print revenue fell 7% to $165M. Print operating profit dropped to $1M from $8M. Management blamed challenging economic conditions, and the quarter's total profit growth came from chemicals.

takeaways.label: Growth slowed
takeaways.text: Total revenue rose only 3%. Operational EBITDA (Kodak's adjusted operating profit) was $31M, versus $36M last quarter and $29M a year ago. Higher silver and aluminum costs and higher SG&A weighed on it.

takeaways.label: Cash and debt
takeaways.text: Cash rose $27M in the quarter to $317M, and year-to-date operating cash flow is about break-even. Interest expense fell to $3M from $18M, lifting net income to $21M.

history.verdict: Kodak's fourth straight year-over-year improvement, with gross profit up 61% and net income of $17 million, now has less debt behind it.

takeaways.label: Margins jumped
takeaways.text: Gross margin rose to 26% from 19% as higher prices and volume outran pricier silver and aluminum. Operational EBITDA reached $36 million, up from $9 million.

takeaways.label: Chemicals led growth
takeaways.text: Advanced Materials & Chemicals revenue rose 40% to $105 million and its operational EBITDA nearly tripled to $22 million. Print grew 10% and swung to an $8 million profit.

takeaways.label: Debt sharply reduced
takeaways.text: Kodak repaid $101 million of term loans and cut interest expense by $9 million. Management said total debt to EBITDA is 1x, versus 23x a year earlier.

takeaways.label: Cash and pension caveats
takeaways.text: Cash fell $47 million to $290 million as inventory rose $37 million on silver and aluminum. Pension income is expected to stay below last year's level through 2026.
